reason: I'll start with the after-meal route: the picture says higher blood glucose triggers insulin release.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release insulin, which may let me follow glucose into muscle next.

alternatives.reason: The lower-glucose route should lead to the liver's message, but I'll follow the meal first.

effect: Insulin is now in the blood, and its route leads toward muscle, so I can follow the after-meal pathway.
reaction: The picture makes the message's destination clear.
reason: I'll combine insulin with muscle to see how it helps the fibres take in glucose.
expectation: I expect the muscle to take in glucose and perhaps store some of it, as the chapter describes.

alternatives.reason: I could start the lower-glucose pathway, but I want to finish following insulin first.

effect: The muscle now has a glucose store, so I'll follow the lower-glucose pathway next.
reaction: It was clear that insulin carries the message rather than becoming part of the store.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the pancreatic cells to release the other hormone into the blood, leading toward the liver store.

effect: The lower-glucose signal produced a hormone that travels to the liver, so I can follow it to the stored carbohydrate.
reaction: The label makes its purpose clear, though the hormone isn't named.
reason: This is the only offered combination and follows the message to the liver store.
expectation: I expect the liver to break down some stored carbohydrate and release glucose into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose from its store into the blood, completing the between-meal pathway. The release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: The shrinking store made the result easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following insulin to muscle was worthwhile because it showed glucose becoming a store while insulin stayed outside as a message.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the liver hormone was less engaging on its own: it was the only offered combination, and the hormone wasn't named.

surprise.text: The liver can release stored glucose into the blood between meals, and the release signal eases as glucose rises.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the last two combinations were guided by the only available options rather than something I figured out myself.

continue.text: I would probably continue: comparing the muscle and liver pathways made the different uses of stored glucose interesting, even though the choices became limited.
